subject: dwarfRifleman
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf rifleman with braided beard and blunderbuss.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a chunky Warcraft-style dwarf rifleman model: broad shoulders, big hands, braided beard, helmet, and a blunderbuss, keeping the module efficient while making sure the API usage stays correct.

Now I'm working through the bone hierarchy — hips as root, a spine chain curving up through chest and neck to the head, with shoulder-elbow-wrist chains for the arms and hip-knee-ankle chains for the legs, mapping out joint names and parent relationships for each segment.

Adding more loft stations for the torso, then settling on a dwarf color palette: blue and gold cloth, leather brown, steel armor, and a red-orange beard fitting the Warcraft dwarf theme.

Now building the legs as three-point joint chains (hip, knee, ankle) with left/right suffixes, and sweeping cylindrical geometry along each leg with a tapering radius function.

For the boots, I'm attaching a box shape at the ankle bone positioned so the foot sits flush with the ground, plus a cylinder cuff near the shin. Then for the arms, I'm placing shoulder joints and considering a rest pose with arms bent outward and down, since one side will grip the gun's stock/trigger and the other the forebarrel.

Settling on a Warcraft-style stance: the blunderbuss held upright with its butt resting on the floor, right hand gripping near the neck of the gun, while the left arm bends at the elbow with the hand resting on the hip/belt. I'm defining joint positions for the right arm's shoulder.

Adjusting the left hand position near the hip, then setting up arm sweep radii with a banded texture transition from blue sleeve to bare skin for the forearm.

Still writing rig helpers for the bracer placement and shoulder pauldrons...

For the head I'm planning the skull sphere, scaled proportions, and face features like nose, brow ridge, and eye decals attached to the head part.

Then I'm designing the massive dwarf beard - thick braided strands hanging from the chin to the chest with beads and ties, built from extruded wedge shapes forming the overall beard mass.

For braids, I'll chain small spheres along a path to simulate strands, attaching them to the head bone so they move naturally with jaw/beard rather than the chest, and plan two braids hanging from the beard sides down toward the chest area.

Still writing braid helper...

For the hat, I'm thinking a dwarven rifleman look with a brimmed steel helmet, lathing a dome profile with a brim and adding a gold crest detail.

Still shaping the feather geometry...

Now I'm planning the dwarf's facial features: pointy cone ears under the hat, a bulbous pink nose, bushy brow boxes angled above the eyes, a moustache hiding the mouth, and a separate lower jaw piece.

Then I'm moving to torso details, figuring out how to construct a belt using a scaled cylinder sized to fit around the waist.

Still working out bandolier placement...

For the tunic I'm planning a blue torso loft with gold trim and an Ironforge-style emblem — a lion or hammer-and-anvil shield decal placed on the chest, though I need to check it doesn't clash with the bandolier crossing over it.

For the gun I'm thinking blunderbuss parts should attach to the wrist-tip bone so it follows the hand naturally, with the butt resting near the floor at y=0 as if held casually.

Working out gun geometry...

Still writing barrel geometry...

Hands need knuckle detail with curled fingers gripping the gun, plus leather glove cuffs. For the lower body I'm planning boots with gold buckles, dark pants, and knee guards, then a cracked stone plinth base with Ironforge-style props like a powder keg nearby.

I'm fleshing out the scene as a dwarf shooting range: a glowing brass lantern, a barrel with banding details, and a practice target with a painted bullseye positioned off to the side to tell the story.

I'll place the target at back-right and the powder keg at back-left to avoid blocking the camera view of the dwarf, and scatter a few small rocks and spent casings for detail. I need to be careful that the base geometry sits flush at y=0 so the model doesn't float or sink through the ground.

Rather than shifting every coordinate by an offset, I'll keep the base extremely thin — just a 0.025 slab, well under the 2% sink tolerance — so the dwarf's feet effectively rest at ground level without reworking all the joint math.

For textures I'm planning around five: eye, emblem, target, keg label, and maybe a small belt buckle detail, skipping the rune strip idea for simplicity. Now I'm moving on to defining the paint colors.

Writing paint functions...

For the braids I'll keep each strand as a flat-colored part to stay under the color budget, then set up small helper functions for vectors, spheres, and placing parts with consistent flat shading options.

Now I'm thinking through the torso loft, deciding how the hip and spine bones should chain together so the body follows a smooth catmull curve without creating a weird zero-length bone at the joint — I'll offset the hips and spine1 positions slightly so the chain starts cleanly.

Then I'm sizing the legs relative to the torso: hip at .62, knee at .34, ankle at .10, keeping proportions stocky and dwarf-like with shorter legs than torso. For the actual geometry I'm sweeping the leg chain with a tapering radius function and setting pants color, planning to do the same approach for the arms.

Now I'm wiring up the shoulder joints, with the arm chain parented to the chest tip of the spine and named for shoulder, elbow, and wrist, tagged with an "arm" role, and hands attached to the wrist bone. For the neck and head I'm setting up joints directly rather than a chain, parenting neck to chest and head to neck with aim directions, adding a jaw joint under the head, then sweeping a rod shape for the neck geometry before defining the head's center position and radius.

Now I'm building the skull as a scaled sphere part attached to the head bone, wrapping it in a surface for decals, and calculating eye placement by projecting onto the sphere's front surface so the eye decals sit correctly in 3D. I'm sketching out the eye SVG with a white almond shape, blue iris, dark outline, and separate bushy brow parts, then placing the nose as a small skin-colored sphere and starting on the brow geometry with mirrored rotation for each side.

Next I'm figuring out brow surface z-placement using the same sphere projection math, then sketching ear cones angled outward from the head and planning the hat as a lathe shape sitting above the head's top point, with a crown radius adjusted to fit the head curvature at that height.

For the hat color, I'm going with brown leather with a gold band and red feather accent, fitting the rifleman theme against the blue tunic. Now moving on to the mustache geometry.

I'm plotting mustache curve points as a catmull-rom spline anchored near the beard bone, checking that the face surface depth lines up correctly for the radius offset so it sits just outside the head mesh. Now I need to work out the beard's bulk extrusion and side outline.

For the front-view extrusion, I'm setting the local axes so x is lateral and y is vertical, with thickness extending along z, then defining the beard's front silhouette points running from the cheeks down past the chin to the jawline, with a thickness parameter controlling depth. I'm positioning the beard's z-depth so it attaches properly at the cheek/jaw surface and extends down in front of the neck and chest.

Now I'm adding sideburn tufts as small scaled spheres near the cheeks, plus a second thinner, lighter extrusion layer offset slightly forward for texture depth, both with slight bevels. Writing grain paint logic...

Then I'm planning two beaded braids hanging from the beard's front, made of small scaled spheres alternating down from y 1.2 to .78, topped with a gold ring and cone tuft, positioned just in front of the main beard surface.

Next I'm checking that the beard layers and braids don't visually clash, deciding to skip adding a mouth element since it's hidden. I'm also sketching a hidden jaw piece bridging the skull and beard, then starting on pauldron shoulder armor using a hemispherical sphere geometry in steel material.

Still writing shoulder geometry...

Adding glove fingers with small stacked spheres plus a thumb, then plotting both arm chains from shoulder through elbow to wrist for each side, bending the elbows outward for a natural pose.

I'm working out where the left hand rests on the belt, checking the belt's elliptical cross-section at the hand's z-height to make sure the hand sphere actually touches the hip rather than floating inside or outside the belt — adjusting the wrist position to [.27,.74,.1] so it makes contact.

Now I'm laying out the torso cross-sections from pelvis up to shoulders with widths and heights at each station, lofting them with a Catmull spline, and adding a slight belly bulge at the waist. I'm also considering whether to add a collar piece — maybe a standing leather collar as a torus around the base of the neck near the shoulders.

Moving to the tunic, I'm adding hanging fabric plates at the front thighs below the belt with gold trim, plus side flaps. For belt accessories, I'm placing pouches at the hips and a curved powder horn swept from the hip upward using a bezier path.

Still building leg details...

Finalizing color list count, then moving to the gun details and the stone slab base, using a lathe profile to create a simple rounded disc shape colored as stone.

Still designing the barrel...

Now I'm figuring out the target stand with wooden posts, a disc base, and a circular target face oriented to face the camera.

For the scene details, I'm adding a few mottled gray rocks, tiny brass spent cartridges near the dwarf's feet, and considering small grass tufts for ground texture.

Then I'm setting up a glowing lantern on the keg with a brass frame, cylindrical body, conical cap, and torus handle ring, giving it a warm orange glow effect.

For the emblem, I'm sketching a shield SVG in blue and gold, trying to decide between a crossed hammer-and-anvil motif or a mountain peak with hammer design.

Next I'm working on a target symbol with concentric red/white/black rings and crosshairs, plus an eye SVG with iris, pupil, and highlight details. I'm also writing a positional helper that interpolates along the gun's barrel direction from butt to tip, accounting for the slight tilt so the frustum box aligns correctly at each segment.

Now I'm defining the gun's bone hierarchy and naming conventions for the arm chains (shoulder, elbow, wrist per side), then building out the stock, brass butt plate, and lock mechanism as tapered frustum boxes with wood and brass/steel coloring.

Placing the lock steel box at the stock-barrel junction, then layering a wood foregrip rod over part of the steel barrel rod so it's intentionally hidden near the breech but exposed further down toward the muzzle bell.

Now I'm adding a brass muzzle rim over the steel bell, plus a small dark interior disc to suggest the bore opening. Working out hammer/cock placement means figuring out the gun's orientation first -- since the dwarf holds it muzzle-up, I need to decide which side faces the body versus which side has the sights, so the trigger and hammer end up on the correct faces.

I'm settling on a lock plate on the outer side and placing the hammer and trigger guard with rough offset coordinates, then adding brass bands around the stock and barrel at a few positions along the length, varying their radius slightly to hug the wood versus the metal barrel.

Now I'm figuring out the fist grip position around the stock, sizing the hand sphere to wrap the wood radius with fingers and thumb offset to either side. Then I'm draping a bandolier sash across the torso using a curved path from shoulder to hip, sweeping a leather tube along it with some lift and bone weighting for drape.

For the cartridges, I'm placing them along the sash path using evenly spaced frames, orienting each cylinder so its axis follows the strap's tangent direction — working through whether that means they lie flat along the strap or stand perpendicular to it like real bullets would.

I'll keep it simple with upright vertical brass cylinders topped with red caps rather than fussing over precise orientation. For the torso, I'm adding blue cloth paint and applying a tabard emblem decal on the front, positioning it so the sash crosses partially over it for a layered look, and I'm considering adding a gold trim loop around the collar.

For the belt, I'm switching from a cylinder to a surface loop cut at the waist height, since it naturally traces around just the torso without catching the arms, then sweeping that loop into a tube for the leather belt -- possibly using a rectangular box cross-section instead of a round one for a more buckled look.

For the buckle, I'm finding the nearest point on the torso surface at the front-center of the belt and sticking a gold box there, embedding it slightly and orienting it along the surface normal so it sits flush against the body.

Now I'm thinking about adding hip tassets—small plate-like boxes placed at the front of the pelvis region, below the torso, to suggest a tabard or kilt detail.

I'm also adding dwarf adventurer gear on the back: a leather backpack box with a bedroll cylinder attached via rope, positioned against the upper back area to balance the character's silhouette.

Now I'm setting up the rig with a root hips joint and spine chain role, then starting the actual code by importing the builder utilities and helper functions needed for the geometry and rigging work.

Setting up material palettes...

Defining the beard paint function to create a streaky reddish-orange color variation along the strands, then setting up sleeve bands that blend cloth color into skin tone along the arm sweep.

Now I'm building the dwarf rifleman skeleton: creating the builder, hip joint, a spine chain with named segments, then resolving the chest as the chain's tip joint. I'm adding the neck, head, and jaw joints with their parent relationships and aim directions, then moving on to the leg joints.

Still writing legs...

Now I'm moving to the torso loft and sash details, then setting up the beard as an extrusion attached to the head bone with a defined thickness and bevel for a rounded edge.

I'm adding a second, narrower beard layer with a lighter paint color to create depth, positioning it slightly forward and shrinking its thickness so it reads as highlighting on top of the base beard shape.

Still placing lantern parts and keg hoops...

Still writing placement logic...
